samples.waterTranscript: I walked through the streets of a submerged city in the middle of a black sea. I could breathe. A door opened in the distance, filled with light from my childhood home.
samples.fallingTranscript: I was falling down an endless staircase but never getting closer to the ground. An enormous moon hung above me. Instead of fear I felt strangely weightless.
samples.teethTranscript: I looked into a mirror in an unfamiliar house. My teeth fell into my hands. I wanted to speak but had no voice. There was only fog outside the window.
samples.neuro: During sleep, memory can bring fragments of the day together with older experiences. Changes in place and feeling can be a starting point for thinking about how memories are reorganized. A dream cannot be assigned one certain meaning.
samples.jung: Read these images through your own associations. A distant place or changing body might be considered a symbol for a need you have not yet named. Ask yourself: what feeling from my waking life does this scene resemble?
samples.astro: You might use the night as a symbolic frame for turning inward and making room for unfinished feelings. No current transit data is available, so this interpretation is not based on any planetary positions.

science.title: Scientific context and reflection
science.scope: General research context · This panel does not send your dream anywhere. Paper links open only when you tap them.
science.limit: Your dream does not measure sleep stage, EEG, neurotransmitter levels or memory transfer percentages. These sources do not validate your personal interpretation.
science.linkError: The source link could not be opened. Try again.
science.symbolicNote: These questions explore personal associations. Jungian symbols are not presented as neurological measurements or experimental evidence.

explanations.memory: Sleep may help retain learned information and integrate it into existing memory networks. Stickgold and Walker review selective processing models of which memories are retained or transformed. This general framework does not determine the meaning of an individual dream.
explanations.emotion: Van der Helm and colleagues reported an association between REM physiology and reduced next-day amygdala responses to previously seen emotional pictures in their sleep group. This specific finding does not show that every dream provides emotional recovery.
explanations.plasticity: Tononi and Cirelli’s synaptic homeostasis hypothesis proposes that sleep may help rebalance synaptic strength altered by learning. This is a general mechanism proposal; a personal synaptic pruning rate cannot be calculated from dream text.
explanations.symbolic: A door, water or a changing body may bring different memories to mind. Rather than assigning one universal meaning, consider your own context. This is a framework for reflection, not a scientific diagnosis.
